transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer orders, my name is Terry. What's the problem?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Terry. I am in complete shock. I moved into my new flat yesterday, took the day off work for the broadband installation engineer who was booked between one and six PM, and nobody showed up! When I checked the online tracker, it says 'Order Cancelled by System' with no notification or explanation whatsoever!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before I look into order status, I have to complete security verification. What is your full name and the move address?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Judith Vance, Flat 4B, St George's Court, Gloucester, GL1 1QZ.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And what is the security PIN on the account, Judith?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What was your former property address where the broadband was moved from?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We moved from 19 Lansdown Road, Cheltenham, GL51 6PT.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And did you submit the home move order online or over the telephone?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Over the telephone two weeks ago with your moves desk.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Bear with me while I access the national address database and Openreach provisioning logs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for waiting, Judith. Looking at the address record for Flat 4B, St George's Court, the property is classified as a commercial mixed-use unit in the Royal Mail Postcode Address File.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's not a commercial unit! It's a completely residential residential apartment in a converted Georgian townhouse!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Openreach automated address bridge rejects residential FTTP orders if the property classification code contains a commercial flag, so that's the conveyancer's and estate agent's fault, not S-Net's.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How is it my conveyancer's fault? The previous tenant had residential S-Net broadband in this exact flat! Why did your system cancel my order without sending me a text message or phone call? I lost a full day of annual leave sitting in an empty flat waiting for an engineer who was never coming!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: System cancellations dispatch email notifications automatically.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I never received an email! Check your mail logs!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: As I said, automated order rejections trigger when wholesale address codes conflict.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you just re-book the engineer for tomorrow so I can get internet for my work?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check where you moved from again. What was that previous address in Cheltenham?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: While we have the wholesale portal open, what type of master socket is installed on the skirting board in the hallway of Flat 4B?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: There is a standard Openreach master socket with an existing optical ONT box on the wall.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What are the LED lights displaying on that optical wall unit?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Power is green, PON is solid green, and LAN is unlit.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: A solid green PON light indicates the physical fibre cable from the street is already spliced and illuminated with live laser light.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right! The physical fibre is already working! So there was zero technical reason to cancel my appointment!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Physical light presence does not override database property classification protocols.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's just mindless bureaucracy.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wholesale telecom providers are legally bound by Ofcom infrastructure separation guidelines.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I don't care about guidelines, I care about moving into my home and having working broadband.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And standard residential billing profiles cannot attach to commercial sub-premises without tariff exception codes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Other tenants in the building have S-Net broadband right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Their units are likely classified as private domestic dwellings on the council tax register.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: My flat is on the council tax register as Band B domestic!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The royal mail database update will require that council tax proof.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I have the council tax bill right here in my moving folder.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can upload it to our web portal under move verification.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I shouldn't have to upload council tax documents just to move my broadband across town.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to confirm for the ombudsman complaint file, your previous address was 19 Lansdown Road, correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, 19 Lansdown Road.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I told you, 19 Lansdown Road, Cheltenham! Why are you asking about my old house when my new flat has no internet?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I cannot re-book an installation until a manual royal mail property classification dispute is submitted to Openreach.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long does that dispute take?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Address classification appeals take seven to ten business days for council planning review.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ten business days? That's two weeks without internet! Why can't you just provision a standard residential broadband order like every other flat in the building?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It's a stupid question to ask why a commercial unit can't have residential broadband without surveyor approval!

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Did you just call my question stupid? How dare you speak to a customer like that!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am stating the regulatory reality. Shouting at me will not rewrite the Postcode Address File.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I want to speak to your manager right now! What is your name and employee ID?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: My name is Terry, operator ID 3810. There is no supervisor available to take escalations.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am lodging an immediate complaint with the telecommunications ombudsman and cancelling my account!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You are free to cancel your pending move order if you wish, Judith.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Cancel it! I am switching to an ISP that treats customers with basic respect!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The pending move order has been ceased on the system.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And am I leaving this call with any working internet at my flat?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, as no installation order is active on the property.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Disgraceful company. Goodbye Terry.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, goodbye.
